newsitem.title: USA: U.S. condemns "paranoid" Libya over balloon flight.
newsitem.headline: U.S. condemns "paranoid" Libya over balloon flight.

text.p: The United States condemned Libya on Friday for refusing permission for a U.S. round-the-world balloon flight to cross its airspace, saying it reflected "paranoia" in the Libyan leadership.

"For the Libyans to say they can't do it reflects the paranoia of the Libyan leadership," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters. "It's really a shame that the Libyans wouldn't have a lighter touch on this one," he said.

He said the U.S. government had not been involved in efforts to persuade Libya to allow the overflight. Washington has no diplomatic relations with Libya, which it accuses of involvment in the bombing of a Pan Am jumbo jet over Lockerbie, Scotland, in 1988.
Burns said U.S. balloonist Steve Fossett should heed the Libyan decision.

"Unfortunately, I suppose, the balloonists must secede to the wishes of the dictators in Tripoli. But it really is unfortunate they didn't have greater vision to see that this would have been an exciting thing for Libya to have been a part of," he said.
After organisers and supporters of the expedition engaged in days of back-channel and public negotiating over the overflight, Libya finally issued a three-line telegram on Friday denying permission.

Project organisers in Chicago said Fossett had decided to make a detour round the north African state but that would use up precious fuel and would most likely force his attempt to fly round the globe to end in India.
